title: Conformal Nature of Quantum Phase Transitions via Fuzzy Three-Sphere Regularization
authors: Xue Meng, Liangdong Hu, Wei Zhu
abstract: Conformal field theory (CFT) offers a modern viewpoint for understanding phase transitions. However, directly accessing the conformal algebra and microscopically uncovering the emergent conformal symmetry, especially in higher dimensions, remains a significant challenge. Motivated by recent advances in revealing CFT features via the fuzzy two-sphere, here we generalize this approach to higher dimensions and aim to expose the conformality at the (3+1)-D quantum critical point. We demonstrate this framework by investigating quantum phase transitions belonging to the Ising and Yang-Lee universality classes in a (3+1)-D quantum model (equivalent to a classical four-dimensional system), realized via Landau level projection on the fuzzy three-sphere. By computing the energy spectra at criticality, we explicitly verify the state-operator correspondence, a hallmark of conformal invariance. Together with prior advances, this work establishes a new pathway for the microscopic study of emergent conformality in higher-dimensional phase transitions.
summary: The paper develops a method using fuzzy three-sphere regularization to analyze quantum phase transitions in (3+1) dimensions. By projecting the system onto Landau levels and comparing computed energy spectra against theoretical CFT predictions, the authors successfully locate critical points for Ising and Yang-Lee models. This establishes a novel pathway for microscopically verifying emergent conformal symmetry in higher-dimensional condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is to expose emergent conformal symmetry at the (3+1)-D quantum critical point, generalizing techniques from fuzzy two-spheres ($S^2$) to higher dimensions.
main_result: The framework successfully maps Quantum Phase Transitions (QPTs) belonging to Ising and Yang-Lee universality classes onto an effective Hamiltonian defined on a fuzzy three-sphere, yielding consistent estimates for critical fields and confirming near-CFT scaling behavior.
method: The study employs radial quantization and utilizes the state-operator correspondence ($\delta E_n \propto \Delta_n$) by minimizing cost functions that compare calculated energy spectra to expected CFT scaling dimensions.
model_or_system: The investigation focuses on (3+1)-D quantum models, specifically the Ising and Yang-Lee transitions, realized through Landau level projection onto the fuzzy three-sphere ($S^3$). The Hamiltonian involves density-density interactions and transverse/longitudinal fields.
key_observables: Energy spectra $\{E_n\}$ at criticality, scaling dimensions ($\Delta_\phi$, $\Delta_{\phi^2}$), and ratios of energy gaps ($R_{1,2}$) used to test for conformal invariance.
important_parameters: The critical fields $h_c$ (for Ising) and $h_z^c$ (for Yang-Lee); the coupling constants defining the Hamiltonian terms.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the successful generalization of spherical background techniques to higher dimensions ($d>2$) and relies on projecting the system into the Lowest Landau Level (LLL) subspace.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Landau levels on $S^3$ derived from $	ext{SO}(5)$ representations, show the evolution of cost functions ($f$ and $F_{\min}$) versus the transverse field $h$, and display operator spectra and ratios confirming CFT structure.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the generalization of fuzzy sphere regularization to $S^3$. It then applies this framework to model QPTs (Ising/Yang-Lee), detailing Hamiltonian construction via LLL projection, followed by calculations using spectral matching cost functions to determine critical points and verify conformal scaling.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful geometric tool—fuzzy geometry on spheres—to study quantum criticality in higher dimensions, linking condensed matter phase transitions directly to the rigorous mathematical structure of Conformal Field Theory.
